rules.title: Record Types for Data Transfer
rules.check: DTOs and Messages MUST be record.

rules.title: Primary Constructors
rules.check: Use Primary Constructors for dependency injection and simple initialization.

rules.title: Pattern Matching
rules.check: Prefer Pattern Matching (is, switch) over as casting.
rules.bad_example:
var btn = sender as Button;
if (btn != null) { ... }

rules.title: Nullable Reference Types
rules.check: Nullable Reference Types MUST be enabled. No implicit nulls.

rules.title: Raw String Literals
rules.check: Use Raw String Literals """ for JSON/SQL/Regex.

rules.title: Required Properties
rules.check: Use required for properties that MUST be set during object init.
rules.bad_example:
public class Config { public string Url { get; set; } }
var c = new Config(); // Url is null!
rules.good_example:
public class Config { public required string Url { get; set; } }
var c = new Config { Url = "..." }; // Compiler enforced

rules.title: Static Abstract Interface Members
rules.check: Use static abstract in interfaces for factories/operators.
rules.bad_example: public interface IFactory<T> { T Create(); } // Instance method
rules.good_example: public interface IFactory<T> { static abstract T Create(); }

rules.title: Implicit Usings
rules.check: Enable Implicit Usings. Remove explicit using System;.

rules.title: Global Usings
rules.check: Common namespaces MUST be in GlobalUsings.cs, not repeated per file.

rules.title: Target-Typed New
rules.check: Use new() when type is evident from declaration.
rules.bad_example: Dictionary<string, List<int>> map = new Dictionary<string, List<int>>();

rules.title: List Patterns
rules.check: Use list patterns for array/list deconstruction and pattern matching.

rules.title: XML Documentation Comments
rules.check: All public and internal classes, interfaces, methods, properties, and fields MUST have XML documentation comments. Include <summary>, <param>, <returns>, and <exception> as appropriate. Private members are excluded.
rules.rationale: XML documentation enables IntelliSense, generates API documentation, and ensures code is self-documenting for team members.
